doc.title: Fred Staton interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 12, 2008

title: From Gospel singer to drums and a carnival minstrel band
summary: He began as a church Gospel singer, got drums in a sponsored church band, and left with a minstrel show band in 1932.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: I started out in the church of course as a Gospel singer. I was the lead singer. And the fellow who was sponsoring us decided that we should have instruments, maybe we should have an orchestra. So he interceded for us to get instruments. Somehow or other, I don’t know how the heck he managed it, right in the middle of the depression with no money or anything, but somehow he managed to get us instruments. And my first instrument was drums. And we played in the church. We had a — what do you call it — one instructor who just instructed us all. There was no individual instruction. So we did that for quite a while, a few months. And meanwhile I was doing this other stuff, porter work and whatever else I could get on the side to make things go. And then there was a group who came through town, a carnival came through town. And they had a minstrel show. And they needed a band to go with this carnival. And that was even before I graduated from high school as a matter of fact, that was in 1932. So I left home with them.
You left home with a minstrel band.

A minstrel band. That was probably the toughest times I’ve ever had in my life. It was tough, really tough. We traveled through Pennsylvania, that’s all. And I’m trying to think how long it was. It wasn’t very long, probably about six weeks at the most. The first stop I remember was in Blairsville, then we went to Connellsville, Ford City and that’s all that’s coming to mind right now.
